name: Camling
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: WALS Online, language Camling (cml): 30 datapoints (features 51A-144S)
sources.note: No stress/rhythm features (14A-17A) coded for Camling.

sources.citation: Ebert, Karen H. 2003. Camling. In G. Thurgood & R. LaPolla (eds.), The Sino-Tibetan Languages, 533-545. London: Routledge (and Ebert 2003 'Kiranti languages: an overview', 505-517, same volume)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress in either chapter; §2 Phonology (533-535) covers segments and CV(C) syllable; only prosodic remark is 'Yes-no questions are marked only by intonation' (p. 544). Overview chapter mentions a possible tonal contrast only for Thulung/Khaling-type languages, not Camling.

sources.citation: Ebert, Karen H. 1997. Camling (Chamling). Languages of the World/Materials 103. München: Lincom Europa. Ch. 1 Phonology, pp. 8-13 (1.1 Consonants, 1.2 Vowels, 1.3 Syllable structure) + p. 6 (Rosetta Project scans, archive.org rosettaproject_rab_phon-1 / _detail-1)
sources.note: Nothing. The complete phonology chapter treats voice, aspiration, palatalization, consonant quantity, vowels, nasalization, diphthongs, syllable structure CV(C); no stress/accent/tone subsection and no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Rai, Bhabindra Kumar. 2019. Chamling basic vowels: acoustic analysis. Gipan 4: 175-185. doi:10.3126/gipan.v4i0.35465
sources.note: Nothing; F0 and formant measurements of six vowels only. Cites Ebert 1997 and Rai 2012 as the articulatory descriptions.

sources.citation: Rai, Tara Mani. 2017. A sociolinguistic survey of Chamling: a Tibeto-Burman language. Report submitted to the Linguistic Survey of Nepal (LinSuN), Central Department of Linguistics, TU. 139 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic survey + 210-word lists. Literature review (pp. 8-9) confirms Rai 2012 grammar covers phonology of the Balamta (Udayapur) speech community.

sources.citation: Chamling, Rana. 2015. Chamling Verb Morphology. MA thesis, Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University (TUCL eLibrary hdl 20.500.14540/16199)
sources.note: Nothing; only verb-stem morphophonology. Bibliography lists Rai V.S. 2012a (Bern PhD), Rai V.S. 2012b Chamling Byakaran, Rai T.B. 2009, Rai Bag Devi 2001 MA thesis.

sources.citation: Chamling, Nabin. 2014. Challenges Faced by Chamling Learners in Learning English. M.Ed. thesis, Tribhuvan University (hdl 20.500.14540/282)
Nepalese Linguistics vols. 26-34 (2011-2019), Digital Himalaya PDFs; grep of full text for Chamling/Camling
sources.note: Chamling appears only in passing citations (nominalization, negation, Puma phonology comparisons); no statement about Chamling stress.

sources.citation: Tumbahang, Govinda Bahadur. 2008. Kiranti people and languages of Nepal. Nepalese Linguistics 23: 408-428 (§4.5 Chamling Rai: consonants, vowels, syllable); Rapacha, Lal. 2008. Notes on the typology of T-B Kiranti languages. Nepalese Linguistics 23: 289-321
sources.note: Nothing on stress for Chamling; Tumbahang gives 30 consonants, 7 vowels, CV(C) syllable; Rapacha discusses phoneme-inventory discrepancies (Ebert 1994 vs 1997 vs Yalungcha 2003) and notes only Kõits and Khaling are tonal among the languages compared.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.) 1909. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. III Part I, 'Rodong or Chamling', pp. 363-365 (based on Hodgson 1857)
sources.note: Nothing; nouns/pronouns/verbs from Hodgson's vocabulary only.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Chamling language'
sources.note: Consonant and vowel tables only; nothing on stress.
